[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.19] (2) In making such an order the court will have regard to—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.19] (a) the means of both parties;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.19] (b) all the circumstances of the case; and

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.19] (c) the need to facilitate access to justice. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.19] (3) If the appeal raises an issue of principle or practice upon which substantial sums may turn, it may not be appropriate to make an order under paragraph (1). [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.19] (4) An application for such an order must be made as soon as practicable and will be determined without a hearing unless the court orders otherwise. ## Orders to limit the recoverable costs of an appeal – appeals in Aarhus Convention claims

## 52.19A

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.19A] (1) In this rule, “Aarhus Convention claim” and “prohibitively expensive” have the same meanings as in Section IX of Part 46, and “claimant” means a claimant to whom rules 46.26 to 46.28 apply. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.19A] (2) In an appeal against a decision made in an Aarhus Convention claim to which rules 46.26 to 46.28 apply, the court must—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.19A] (a) consider whether the costs of the proceedings will be prohibitively expensive for a party who was a claimant; and

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.19A] (b) if they will be, make an order limiting the recoverable costs to the extent necessary to prevent this. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.19A] (3) When the court considers the financial resources of a party for the purposes of this rule, it must have regard to any financial support which any person has provided or is likely to provide to that party. ## Appeal court’s powers

## 52.20

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (1) In relation to an appeal the appeal court has all the powers of the lower court. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (Rule 52.1(4) provides that this Part is subject to any enactment that sets out special provisions with regard to any particular category of appeal. Where such an enactment gives a statutory power to a tribunal, person or other body, it may be the case that the appeal court may not exercise that power on an appeal.)

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (2) The appeal court has power to—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (a) affirm, set aside or vary any order or judgment made or given by the lower court;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (b) refer any claim or issue for determination by the lower court;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (c) order a new trial or hearing;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (d) make orders for the payment of interest;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (e) make a costs order. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (3) In an appeal from a claim tried with a jury the Court of Appeal may, instead of ordering a new trial—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (a) make an order for damages; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (b) vary an award of damages made by the jury. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (4) The appeal court may exercise its powers in relation to the whole or part of an order of the lower court. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (Part 3 contains general rules about the court’s case management powers.)

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (5) If the appeal court—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (a) refuses an application for permission to appeal;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (b) strikes out an appellant’s notice; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (c) dismisses an appeal,

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] and it considers that the application, the appellant’s notice or the appeal is totally without merit, the provisions of paragraph (6) must be complied with. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (6) Where paragraph (5) applies—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (a) the court’s order must record the fact that it considers the application, the appellant’s notice or the appeal to be totally without merit; and

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.20] (b) the court must at the same time consider whether it is appropriate to make a civil restraint order. ## Hearing of appeals

## 52.21

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.21] (1) Every appeal will be limited to a review of the decision of the lower court unless—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.21] (a) a practice direction makes different provision for a particular category of appeal; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.21] (b) the court considers that in the circumstances of an individual appeal it would be in the interests of justice to hold a re-hearing. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.21] (2) Unless it orders otherwise, the appeal court will not receive—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.21] (a) oral evidence; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.21] (b) evidence which was not before the lower court. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.21] (3) The appeal court will allow an appeal where the decision of the lower court was—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.21] (a) wrong; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.21] (b) unjust because of a serious procedural or other irregularity in the proceedings in the lower court. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.21] (4) The appeal court may draw any inference of fact which it considers justified on the evidence. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.21] (5) At the hearing of the appeal, a party may not rely on a matter not contained in that party’s appeal notice unless the court gives permission. ## Non-disclosure of Part 36 offers and payments

## 52.22

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.22] (1) Unless the appeal court otherwise orders, the fact that a Part 36 offer or payment into court has been made must not be disclosed to any judge of the appeal court who is to hear or determine—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.22] (a) an application for permission to appeal

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.22] (b) an appeal;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.22] until all questions (other than costs) have been determined. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.22] (2) Paragraph (1) does not apply if the Part 36 offer or payment into court is relevant to the substance of the appeal. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.22] (3) Paragraph (1) does not prevent disclosure in any application in the appeal proceedings if disclosure of the fact that a Part 36 offer or payment into court has been made is properly relevant to the matter to be decided. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.22] (Rule 36.4 has the effect that a Part 36 offer made in proceedings at first instance will not have consequences in any appeal proceedings. Therefore, a fresh Part 36 offer needs to be made in appeal proceedings. However, this rule applies to a Part 36 offer whether made in the original proceedings or in the appeal.)

## V SPECIAL PROVISIONS RELATING TO THE COURT OF APPEAL

## Assignment of appeals to the Court of Appeal

## 52.23

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.23] (1) Where the court from or to which an appeal is made or from which permission to appeal is sought (“the relevant court”) considers that—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.23] (a) an appeal which is to be heard by the County Court or the High Court would raise an important point of principle or practice; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.23] (b) there is some other compelling reason for the Court of Appeal to hear it,

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.23] the relevant court may order the appeal to be transferred to the Court of Appeal. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.23] (The Master of the Rolls has the separate statutory power to direct that an appeal which would be heard by the County Court or the High Court should be heard instead by the Court of Appeal – see section 57 of the Access to Justice Act 1999 4 .)

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.23] (2) The Master of the Rolls or the Court of Appeal may remit an appeal to the court in which the original appeal was or would have been brought. ## Who may exercise the powers of the Court of Appeal

## 52.24

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (1) A court officer assigned to the Civil Appeals Office who is—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (a) a barrister; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (b) a solicitor; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (c) a Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Legal Executives or a CILEX lawyer,

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] may exercise the jurisdiction of the Court of Appeal with regard to the matters set out in paragraph (2) with the consent of the Master of the Rolls. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (2) The matters referred to in paragraph (1) are—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (a) any matter incidental to proceedings in the Court of Appeal;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (b) any other matter where there is no substantial dispute between the parties; and

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (c) the dismissal of an appeal or application where a party has failed to comply with any order, rule or practice direction. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (3) A court officer may not decide an application for—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (a) permission to appeal;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (b) bail pending an appeal;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (c) an injunction ( GL ) ;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (d) a stay ( GL ) of execution of any order or decision of the lower court other than a temporary stay over a period when the Court of Appeal is not sitting or cannot conveniently be convened;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (e) a stay of proceedings in the lower court. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (4) Decisions of a court officer will be made without an oral hearing, unless a court officer directs otherwise. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (5) A party may request any decision of a court officer to be reviewed by a single judge, and—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (a) the review will be determined on paper without an oral hearing; except that

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (b) the judge determining the review on paper may direct that the review be determined at an oral hearing, and must so direct if the judge is of the opinion that the review cannot be fairly determined on paper without an oral hearing. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (6) A party may request a decision of a single judge made without a hearing (other than a decision made on a review under paragraph (5) and a decision determining an application for permission to appeal) to be reconsidered, and—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (a) the reconsideration will be determined by the same or another judge on paper without an oral hearing; except that

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (b) the judge determining the reconsideration on paper may direct that the reconsideration be determined at an oral hearing, and must so direct if the judge is of the opinion that the reconsideration cannot be fairly determined on paper without an oral hearing. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (7) A request under paragraph (5) or (6) must be filed within 7 days after the party is served with notice of the decision. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (8) A single judge may refer any matter for a decision by a court consisting of two or more judges. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (Section 54(4) of the Access to Justice Act 1999 5 provides that there is no appeal from the decision of a single judge on an application for permission to appeal.)

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (Section 58(2) of the Senior Courts Act 1981 6 provides that there is no appeal to the Supreme Court from decisions of the Court of Appeal that—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (a) are taken by a single judge or any officer or member of staff of that court in proceedings incidental to any cause or matter pending before the civil division of that court; and

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] (b) do not involve the determination of an appeal or of an application for permission to appeal,

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.24] and which may be called into question by rules of court. Paragraphs (5) and (6) of this rule provide the procedure for the calling into question of such decisions.)

## VI SPECIAL PROVISIONS RELATING TO STATUTORY APPEALS

## Statutory appeals – court’s power to hear any person

## 52.25

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.25] (1) In a statutory appeal any person may apply for permission—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.25] (a) to file evidence; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.25] (b) to make representations at the appeal hearing. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.25] (2) An application under paragraph (1) must be made promptly. ## Appeals under the Law of Property Act 1922

[PART 52 – APPEALS > Appeals under the Law of Property Act 1922] 52.26 An appeal lies to the High Court against a decision of the Secretary of State under paragraph 16 of Schedule 15 to the Law of Property Act 1922 7 . ## Appeals from certain tribunals

## 52.27

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.27] (1) A person who was a party to proceedings before a tribunal referred to in section 11(1) of the Tribunals and Inquiries Act 1992 8 and is dissatisfied in point of law with the decision of the tribunal may appeal to the High Court. (2) The tribunal may, on its own initiative or at the request of a party to the proceedings before it, state, in the form of a special case for the decision of the High Court, a question of law arising in the course of the proceedings. ## Appeals under certain planning legislation

## 52.28

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] (1) Where the Secretary of State has given a decision in proceedings on an appeal under Part VII of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 9 against an enforcement notice—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] (a) the appellant;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] (b) the local planning authority; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] (c) another person having an interest in the land to which the notice relates,

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] may appeal to the High Court against the decision on a point of law. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] (2) Where the Secretary of State has given a decision in proceedings on an appeal under Part VIII of that Act against a notice under section 207 of that Act—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] (a) the appellant;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] (b) the local planning authority; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] (c) another person (other than the appellant) on whom the notice was served,

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] may appeal to the High Court against the decision on a point of law. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] (3) Where the Secretary of State has given a decision in proceedings on an appeal under section 39 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 10 against a listed building enforcement notice—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] (a) the appellant;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] (b) the local planning authority; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] (c) any other person having an interest in the land to which the notice relates,

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.28] may appeal to the High Court against the decision on a point of law. ## Appeals under certain legislation relating to pensions

## 52.29 Where an appeal lies to the High Court—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.29 Where an appeal lies to the High Court—] (a) under section 151(4) of the Pension Schemes Act 1993 11 from a determination or direction of the Pensions Ombudsman; or

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.29 Where an appeal lies to the High Court—] (b) under section 217(1) of the Pensions Act 2004 12 from a determination or direction of the Pension Protection Fund Ombudsman, the permission of the High Court is required for such an appeal to be brought. ## VII REOPENING FINAL APPEALS

## Reopening of final appeals

## 52.30

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.30] (1) The Court of Appeal or the High Court will not reopen a final determination of any appeal unless—

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.30] (a) it is necessary to do so in order to avoid real injustice;

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.30] (b) the circumstances are exceptional and make it appropriate to reopen the appeal; and

[PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.30] (c) there is no alternative effective remedy. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.30] (2) In paragraphs (1), (3), (4) and (6), “appeal” includes an application for permission to appeal. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.30] (3) This rule does not apply to appeals to the County Court. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.30] (4) Permission is needed to make an application under this rule to reopen a final determination of an appeal even in cases where under rule 52.3(1) permission was not needed for the original appeal. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.30] (5) There is no right to an oral hearing of an application for permission unless, exceptionally, the judge so directs. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.30] (6) The judge must not grant permission without directing the application to be served on the other party to the original appeal and giving that party an opportunity to make representations. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.30] (7) There is no right of appeal or review from the decision of the judge on the application for permission, which is final. [PART 52 – APPEALS > 52.30] (8) The procedure for making an application for permission is set out in Practice Direction 52A. ## Footnotes
